dedupe_keys.name: ntia its low frequency medium frequency lf mf propagation model

description: The LF/MF model of the Institute for Telecommunication Sciences of the US National Telecommunications and Information Administration predicts basic transmission loss in the frequency range 0.01 to 30 MHz for ground-wave propagation paths over a smooth Earth with antenna heights below 50 metres, the regime of AM broadcasting, LF time signals and navigation beacons. ITS publishes a C++ reference implementation built as a shared library, a command-line driver with plain-text input and output files, and bindings for .NET, MATLAB and Python, all part of the ITS Propagation Library (PropLib); a separate repository holds test data. Coverage: any path over a smooth Earth, with ground conductivity and permittivity as inputs. Format and access: source code on GitHub and a citable Zenodo archive (version 1.1, CC-BY-4.0 on Zenodo), with documentation on the PropLib wiki and Doxygen pages; as a US Government work it has no copyright in the US and comes with the NTIA disclaimer. Caveats: smooth-Earth only, so terrain and mixed paths are not modelled; ionospheric sky-wave is outside its scope. Simulation uses: coverage and hazard exposure of AM and LF broadcast and emergency alerting, and spectrum planning. Related records: ITS ITM covers 20 MHz to 20 GHz, and eHata, P.528 and P.2108 are other PropLib models.
